start.text: Report sent. A look-alike domain made two days ago, a link that says one thing and goes to another, and one password typed.
start.name: Joshua

A.text: Joshua, I read your report. A fake does not need to be clever. It needs to look official and be in a hurry.
A.name: Carla

B.text: So tonight you read each email as it arrives.
B.name: Carla

C1.text: The [b][color=green]rulebook[/color][/b] has it: the sender's domain, where the link really goes, and what it asks. Never how it looks.
C1.name: Carla

C2.text: No. HR and IT send links too, and they are real. We check where each link goes.
C2.name: Carla

D.text: [b][color=red]Report[/color][/b] the fakes. Let the rest [b][color=green]pass[/color][/b], even the ones that look official.
D.name: Carla

E.text: One email at a time. A fake can look perfect, and a real one can look odd.
E.name: Joshua
